description: Which of the two codes a boundary-hidden read gets is decided LEXICALLY, not temporally (spec/execution-model.md:405-414, spec/error-model.md:132): "a name an enclosing scope binds anywhere in the declaring document takes this code whether or not that binding has been created by the time the read executes". Here `peek` runs BEFORE `:later = 1` has executed, so no binding of `later` exists anywhere at that instant — yet the code is still `ol-var-not-visible`, naming the boundary, because the root scope binds the name somewhere in the document. That is what keeps the code decidable at the `semantic` stage and what lets issue #825's checker report the same identity the runtime does instead of contradicting it on execution order. A runtime that asked the temporal question ("is it bound yet?") would report `ol-undefined-var` here and disagree with its own checker.

diagnostics.message: :later is not defined inside peek. a procedure only sees its own inputs, the names it sets itself, and names declared global. the fix is one word at the top level: write global later = (its starting value).
